text:
sam: noticing steady memory growth on a few prod hosts after long-context jobs (~30k tokens). eviction rate stays constant but fragmentation climbs, we're seeing a 12-18% decrease in usable KV pool over 48h :thinking:
anya: hmm, same hosts as last week's rollout?
sam: different cluster. kernel selection change last week (new fused-attn kernel) + batching tweaks. profiler shows more small free blocks (~64B-4KB) accumulating in the slab allocator.
kai: could be allocator hole creation from long KV chains + frequent evictions. any recent change to block-size rounding or reuse policy?
anya: we changed the reuse threshold from 0.75->0.65 in 1749800000 deploy to favor reuse across requests. might be interacting poorly with page-aligned batching.
sam: timeline matches. Also observed that when batching latency spikes, the runtime issues partial evictions which leave behind tiny fragments.
rachel: quick idea — instead of immediate one-shot compaction, schedule a short background "reshuffle" that coalesces adjacent free slots within a shard when CPU idle. do incremental moves capped by ms budget to avoid p99 regressions.
kai: agree. we need heuristics to pick shards: prefer shards with high fragmentation score (free_count weighted by block-size variance) and low recent traffic. sampling-based detector would avoid scanning hot shards.
anya: draft heuristic: fragmentation_score = (1 - largest_free_run_fraction) * log(1 + free_block_count) * recent_eviction_rate. threshold 0.6 triggers reshuffle job.
nanny-bot (kv-bot): scheduled background compaction jobs should enforce max-moves-per-second and backoff if latency > SLO.
sam: what about block-size tuning? maybe switch small allocations to a segregated arena (tiny pool) to reduce cross-size fragmentation. we already do slab classes but the cross-request reuse policy might be mixing sizes.
kai: segregated tiny arena + age-based reclamation could help. also consider bumping minimum block size from 64->128 for the general allocator, keep tiny pool for sub-128 allocations. that reduces bookkeeping overhead.
rachel: implementation sketch: 1) fragmentation sampler (per-shard, low-cost), 2) reshuffle worker with ms budget and rate limit, 3) tiny-pool segregation change behind feature flag.
anya: before rollout, let's run a perf job: long-context replay (30k tokens) x48h on staging with new heuristics and collect: fragmentation %, eviction count, p50/p95 latency.
sam: I'll open a perf run and add a quick CLI to force-run reshuffle on a shard for testing.

sam: CLI prototype:
```
# force a reshuffle on shard 3 with 50ms budget
kvctl reshuffle --shard=3 --budget-ms=50 --dry-run
```

kai: also add metrics: reshuffle_moves, reshuffle_aborts_due_to_latency, fragment_coalesced_bytes.
anya: if staging looks good, we can try a canary rollout to one host pool with aggressive reshuffle and monitor token cost impact.
rachel: thanks — this approach keeps compaction incremental and avoids big GC pauses. set up a follow-up thread with perf logs and we can iterate on threshold. :thumbsup:
kv-bot: created ticket #INF-4762 "incremental reshuffle compaction and tiny-pool segregation"
